newsitem.title: IRAN: Iran troops ready for U.S., not on alert - official.
newsitem.headline: Iran troops ready for U.S., not on alert - official.

text.p: An Iranian military official said on Tuesday Iran's armed forces were ready to face any threats but denied they had been placed on alert against a possible attack by the United States.

Earlier on Tuesday, a member of parliament spoke about Iranian armed forces having been put on alert against the perceived threat of a possible U.S. strike linked to a truck bomb attack that killed 19 U.S. airmen in Saudi Arabia in June.

Asked to comment on the deputy's remarks, an official at Iran's Armed Forces Joint Chiefs of Staff told Reuters: "Our armed forces are ready to defend the territory of the Islamic Republic. But there is no alert of the kind you are thinking of."

The deputy, Mohammad Baqer Nobakht, said in a parliamentary debate broadcast live on Tehran radio: "You all heard last month the threat made...by America. You all heard about our armed forces being put on alert."
Nobakht was referring to Western media reports linking Iran to the Saudi explosion. Iran has not been officially linked to the bombing and it has repeatedly denied any role in the attack.

Iranian officials have said the media reports indicated that the United States was preparing an attack on Iran. Diplomats have said Washington may strike at Iran if it is convinced that Tehran played a role in the bombing.
